idea_name: CNN-LSTM close sequence sensor with D1 MinMax and UP/SAME/DOWN class
mechanism: Train Conv1D(256,k=2)+MaxPool+2×LSTM(100)+Dense(sigmoid) on MinMax-scaled EURUSD H1 closes with lookback 120; at inference normalize the 120 H1 closes by the rolling 120 D1 close min/max, OnnxRun, denormalize predicted close, then classify vs last close with |delta|<=1e-5 → SAME else UP/DOWN.
data_needed: EURUSD H1 closes (120-bar window) plus concurrent 120 D1 closes for ExtMin/ExtMax; ONNX CNN-LSTM weights.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 (primary); EURUSD D1 used only for MinMax bounds; referenced stock daily features OHLC/volume/turnover/change in cited paper.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a deployable MQL5 sequence sensor that couples H1 path shape to a slower D1 range scale and emits an explicit three-way directional label rather than a raw price point.
quote: we choose eight features, including opening price, highest price, lowest price, closing price, volume, turnover, ups and downs, and change. Firstly, we adopt CNN to efficiently extract features from the data, which are the items of the previous 10 days. And then, we adopt LSTM to predict the stock price

idea_name: Unanimous voting ensemble of OHLC-LSTM regression and 63-close MLP classifier
mechanism: Model1: LSTM(64) on 10 normalized OHLC bars predicts next close; denormalize; map delta vs last close with |delta|<=0.0001 to PRICE_UP/SAME/DOWN. Model2: Dense MLP on 63 z-scored closes softmaxes three classes. Predict() sets ExtPredictedClass only when both models emit the same class; else -1 (no trade).
data_needed: EURUSD D1 OHLC (10 bars) and Close (63 bars); per-window mean/std normalization; two ONNX models.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; training windows 2003–2022 (regression) and 2010–2022 (classification); out-of-sample from 2023.
why_new_for_mis: MIS can treat model agreement itself as a gate on a directional neural sensor—disagreement is an explicit abstain, not a weak vote average.
quote: A class is considered selected when both models have received the same class. This is a majority vote. And since there are only two models in the ensemble, voting by the majority means "unanimous".

idea_name: Three-class price-move regime with flat band (±10 points / 0.0001)
mechanism: Classification target and live mapping use three regimes: down, same (abs(delta)<=0.0001 on 5-digit EURUSD, i.e. 10 points), up. Flat band was forced by 4→5 digit quote change; model abstains from directional action when SAME or when ensemble disagrees.
data_needed: Next-bar close vs last close in the input window; fixed flat threshold 0.0001 (or instrument-specific point band).
why_new_for_mis: Encodes a tradable flat/noise regime as a first-class label alongside up/down, which MIS can use as a no-edge / range sensor rather than forcing binary direction.
quote: One of three classes must be defined at the output: the price will go down, the price will stay within 10 points, or the price will go up.

mechanism: Canvas demo of affine fit and secant→tangent limit (h→0) as the learning step; no market features or sensors built.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing content after full read—pure educational math for NN training.
quote: The main purpose is not to create a system oriented towards the market or some specific task.

mechanism: Manual/automatic least-squares minimization of squared residuals for slope (and later intercept shift); charting pedagogy only.
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing—continues NN math pedagogy.
quote: finding a straight line function through a loop is not as easy as it seemed.

idea_name: General least-squares and pseudoinverse tutorial only
mechanism: Closed-form a,b for y=ax+b and Moore–Penrose pinv sketch for polynomial fit; no market application.
quote: what we'll see here is for a neural network that won't be receiving any new information into its database.

idea_name: Multi-explainer feature-importance consensus as indicator sensor
mechanism: After CatBoostRegressor on Volatility 75 Index M1 with EMA/BB/RSI/ATR/AO/MACD/CCI/KST/TSI/ROC/DM features and target=close.shift(-30), rank features via RFE drop-column, ELI5 permutation importance, SHAP TreeExplainer, and mutual_info_regression; keep consensus leaders (OHLC, EMAs, Bollinger components) and drop the rest.
data_needed: OHLCV + pandas_ta indicators listed in predictors; train/test chronological split; sklearn/eli5/shap MI scores.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Volatility 75 Index, M1 (~100k bars); target horizon 30 bars ahead.
why_new_for_mis: Turns post-hoc XAI agreement into a sensing layer that selects which technical channels actually move a black-box forecast—usable as a live feature gate for MIS.
quote: We observe a consistent consensus across all our black-box explanation techniques, suggesting that features consistently highlighted in these explanations likely contain substantial information

idea_name: Hybrid OHLC linear + CatBoost residual sensor
mechanism: Fit LinearRegression on open/high/low/close to target; fit CatBoost on residuals using only BBM/BBL/BBU and ema_20/40/100; live forecast = lm_pred + cat_residual. Reported ~94% MSE reduction vs full-feature CatBoost and removed unnatural flat tree plateaus.
data_needed: Normalized OHLC plus Bollinger mid/low/up and three EMAs; two-stage train (linear then residual booster).
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a practical decomposition: linear price level sensor plus nonlinear residual sensor on smoothed band/EMA state—cleaner than a single extrapolating tree.
quote: Our new black-box hybrid has error metrics that have improved by 94%.

idea_name: 2D PDP of ROC×ATR as volatility–momentum response surface
mechanism: PartialDependenceDisplay on CatBoost for joint (ROC_10, ATRr_14) shows that rising ROC and ATR together lift expected close forecast, but with unstable mixed enclaves—use the surface (or its gradient) as a volatility-conditioned momentum sensor.
data_needed: ROC_10 and ATR(14) aligned with the trained regressor; PDP grid over test subset.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Volatility 75 Index M1; ATR length 14, ROC length 10.
why_new_for_mis: Explicitly couples a volatility proxy (ATR) with rate-of-change into a model-response sensor rather than treating ATR as a standalone filter.
quote: an increase in both the ROC (Rate of Change) and ATR (Average True Range) indicators corresponds to an increase in the expected prediction from our model.

mechanism: Educational MQL5 array-based matrix multiply, transpose product, Sarrus determinant toward PInv; compares to matrix.PInv().
quote: I don't want to give false expectations: I'm not going to tell you that with virtually no knowledge or experience you can create something really practical that can be used to make money

idea_name: ALE response curves as correlation-robust feature→price sensors
mechanism: Train DNN/XGB on scaled OHLC+MA20+RSI60+CCI10+AO+BB(120)+ATR14 with Target=Close.shift(-30); compute Accumulated Local Effects (alibi ALE). Downward-sloping ALE for Awesome Oscillator ⇒ rising AO associated with lower forecasted close; flat ALE (e.g. RSI) ⇒ uninformative.
data_needed: Indicator panel from MQL5 CSV export; scaled features; ALE explainer on model.predict.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MT5 symbol PERIOD_CURRENT in fetch script; case-study bars with MA/RSI/CCI/AO/BBands/ATR; NFL toy dataset also used for pedagogy.
why_new_for_mis: ALE gives MIS a marginal-effect sensor that remains usable when technical features are strongly correlated—unlike naive permutation/SHAP independence assumptions.
quote: ALE extends on all the explanative techniques we have considered so far because it is robust and can handle strongly correlated features, it relaxes assumptions of feature independence

mechanism: Compare black-box vs white-box SHAP, eli5 vs sklearn permutation importance, MI, Morris sensitivity, and native XGB importance on the same model; treat rank/sign flips and input-order sensitivity as a disagreement score. High disagreement ⇒ low trust in feature attributions / unstable sensing stack; prefer GAMs/EBMs when disagreement dominates.
data_needed: Same trained model + multiple explainers; optional feature-order shuffles.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Market CSV from MT5 indicators; Madden NFL toy data for controlled disagreement demos.
why_new_for_mis: MIS can monitor disagreement across explainers as a sensor of attribution instability—useful before promoting any feature-importance-based regime detector.
quote: the disagreement problem is a key area of research within Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)… we cannot blindly trust any explanation we may get
